question: A 25 kg child needs maintenance IV fluids. Using the Holliday-Segar method, what is the correct 24-hour maintenance fluid volume?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 1500 mL/day is the volume for a 20 kg child (100×10 + 50×10 = 1500). A 25 kg child requires an additional 20 mL for each kg above 20 kg.
Correct. Holliday-Segar: 100 mL/kg for first 10 kg (1000 mL) + 50 mL/kg for next 10 kg (500 mL) + 20 mL/kg for each kg above 20 kg (5 × 20 = 100 mL) = 1600 mL/day.
This does not correspond to the Holliday-Segar formula for 25 kg. Check: 100×10 + 50×10 + 20×5 = 1000 + 500 + 100 = 1600 mL/day.
2500 mL/day incorrectly applies a flat 100 mL/kg to the total body weight. The Holliday-Segar method uses a stepped rate: 100/50/20 mL/kg/day, not a uniform rate across all weight.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Holliday-Segar method: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for every kilogram above 20 kg.
Well done. The Holliday-Segar 100/50/20 rule is the standard method for estimating daily maintenance fluid requirements in children. For 25 kg: 1000 + 500 + 100 = 1600 mL/day.
